_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the melting point of n-eicosane with the MACE-MPA-0 force field.

payload.reason: Premise and validation checks failed: MACE-MPA-0 is outside its domain for the intermolecular (van der Waals) interactions that set the melting point of a paraffin molecular crystal, so any MD melting point would reflect a model artifact rather than eicosane. (1) Independent known result NOT recovered: on the S22 methane dimer (CCSD(T) reference about -0.53 kcal/mol = -2.2 kJ/mol, Jurecka et al. 2006 S22 set, ASE s22 geometry), MACE-MPA-0 gives -46.5 kJ/mol, about 20x overbinding; the S22 ethene dimer gives -30.8 kJ/mol. (2) For two parallel all-trans eicosane chains (unrelaxed, 4.0 A interchain distance), MACE-MPA-0 gives a pair binding energy of -265 kJ/mol. That one pair already exceeds eicosane's whole measured sublimation enthalpy (170.4 kJ/mol, NIST WebBook, Morawetz 1972), even though each chain in the crystal has about 6 neighbors. So the model's lattice cohesion is several times too strong, and its predicted Tm would be badly overestimated, or the system would not melt cleanly at all. MPA-0 was trained on periodic PBE/PBE+U inorganic data (MPtrj + sAlex) with no dispersion and essentially no molecular-crystal data. A fine-tuned or D3 add-on would not fix an overbinding baseline. (3) Even with a sound model, a converged coexistence Tm for C20 needs about 100+ molecules (about 6000+ atoms) and multi-ns runs at several temperatures, which is far beyond this run's budget. Proposed well-posed alternative: use a potential validated for alkane intermolecular energies (e.g. a molecular MLIP such as MACE-OFF, or a TraPPE-UA/L-OPLS classical force field). First recover the measured Tm of n-octadecane (301.0 +/- 0.7 K) or n-hexadecane (291.0 +/- 1.0 K) from /data/calibration/tier1.json with the same solid-liquid interface coexistence protocol (NPT, about 100 molecules, at least 2 ns per temperature, bracketing temperatures 2-5 K apart). Then run eicosane (measured 310.0 +/- 1.0 K, used only as an a-posteriori check) and report the bracket half-width plus the validation offset as the uncertainty.

details.caveat: Eicosane dimer geometry is idealized and unrelaxed, so the scan is semi-quantitative; the S22 test uses reference geometries and is the decisive validation.
